recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-12813 unless a work group separately decides to add generic Request-pattern delegation guidance as a new, broader decision.
issue_request: FHIR-12813 asked for RequestOnBehalfOf, RequestedBy, or requestSubmittedBy support on DSTU2 DiagnosticRequest and MedicationPrescription so systems could capture staff entering a request on behalf of an ordering clinician. The Published Not Persuasive with Modification resolution rejected a new core element or core extension because Provenance handles intermediaries, allowed implementer extensions, and asked for requester comments clarifying that delegation is generally managed through Provenance.
initial_application: The explicit implementation commit 8f78b25c34a539d54ff592c1cfae64b716381bfd, titled "[#12905], [#12813]", added the approved delegation/Provenance sentence to ProcedureRequest.requester. That historical DiagnosticRequest/ProcedureRequest lineage is now represented by ServiceRequest, where the comment is still present. No FHIR-12813-tagged MedicationRequest commit was found; MedicationRequest had already been shaped by Pharmacy workflow issue FHIR-10456 with requester choices and recorder/on-behalf workflow semantics.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists request, medicationrequest, and servicerequest as active current-build artifacts. Current ServiceRequest.requester states that requester is the authorizer, not dispatcher, and that delegation is generally managed through Provenance. Current MedicationRequest.requester identifies the activation-responsible requester, while MedicationRequest.recorder captures the person who entered the order on behalf of another. The FHIR-12813 resolution mentioned creating a tracker to consider adding guidance to the request pattern, but no final linked tracker or community record was found requiring a broader current-core change.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and made no source edits. Adding a duplicate MedicationRequest requester comment or a broad Request-pattern rule would not improve the current specification and could create drift with MedicationRequest.recorder semantics.

related_jiras.note: Pharmacy's published MedicationRequest workflow change added requester choices and recorder/on-behalf workflow, explaining why MedicationRequest does not need the same ServiceRequest requester comment.
This unrelated ProcedureRequest.code cardinality issue was applied in the same historical commit as FHIR-12813 but was not investigated or decided here.
